# hubspot_reports (Data Source)

Lists HubSpot reports matching optional filters (all filters combine with AND; within a set filter, any value matches). Typical use: snapshot every report's metadata to git with `local_file` and `for_each` over the results, find orphaned reports with `on_dashboard = false`, or feed `ids` into `import` blocks to adopt them as `hubspot_report` resources. Every page of results is fetched (100 per request, following the pagination cursor).

`raw_json` holds the API object canonicalized — sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline — with the volatile view-tracking fields (`lastViewedAt`, `lastViewedByUserId`) stripped. It is meant for **committed snapshots** (write it with `local_file` and check it into git): a snapshot only diffs on real changes, and fields HubSpot adds to the API later are captured without a provider release. The typed `last_viewed_at` / `last_viewed_by_user_id` attributes still expose the view-tracking values.

**Report configuration (query, data sources, filters, visualization) is not exposed by the HubSpot API at all** — not even readable — so it cannot be captured here; only metadata, permissions, tags and dashboard layout are. Exporting report data (the API's emailed CSV/PDF export) is intentionally not offered: it is a side-effecting action on CRM record data, outside this provider's configuration-plane scope.

**The Analytics Reporting API is a public beta** (`/analytics/reporting/2027-03-beta`), so this is beta-backed per the provider's [API stability policy](https://github.com/revosai/terraform-provider-hubspot/blob/main/ROADMAP.md#api-stability-policy). The portal must opt into the beta (via the associated product update in HubSpot) and the token needs the `reporting.full.read` scope (plus `reporting.full.write` to create, clone or archive).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# All reports on a given dashboard.
data "hubspot_dashboard" "sales" {
  name = "Sales overview"
}

data "hubspot_reports" "on_sales_dashboard" {
  dashboard_id = data.hubspot_dashboard.sales.id
}

# Orphaned reports (on no dashboard): candidates for clean-up.
data "hubspot_reports" "orphaned" {
  on_dashboard = false
}

output "orphaned_report_names" {
  value = [for r in data.hubspot_reports.orphaned.reports : r.name]
}

# Snapshot every report's metadata (permissions, tags, owner, ...) to git,
# one file per report keyed by ID.
data "hubspot_reports" "all" {}

resource "local_file" "report_snapshot" {
  for_each = { for r in data.hubspot_reports.all.reports : r.id => r }

  filename = "${path.module}/reporting/reports/${each.key}.json"
  content  = each.value.raw_json
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) When `true`, returns archived reports **instead of** active ones (mirrors the API's `archived` parameter). Defaults to `false`.
- `business_unit_ids` (Set of String) Only reports in one of these business units (`0` is the default business unit).
- `dashboard_id` (String) Only reports shown on this dashboard (by dashboard ID).
- `on_dashboard` (Boolean) When `true`, only reports that are on at least one dashboard; when `false`, only reports on no dashboard (handy for finding orphaned reports). Unset returns both.
- `owner_user_ids` (Set of String) Only reports owned by one of these HubSpot user IDs.
- `query` (String) Only reports whose name **or description** contains this text (case-insensitive, HubSpot's `q` search).
- `tag_ids` (Set of String) Only reports carrying at least one of these tag IDs.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable identifier for this data source: `reports`, followed by the non-default filter arguments as a sorted, URL-encoded query string (e.g. `reports?query=sales`).
- `ids` (List of String) IDs of the matching reports, in result order (ascending numeric ID).
- `reports` (Attributes List) The matching reports, ordered by ascending numeric ID. Each item has the same attributes as the `hubspot_report` data source, including its own `raw_json` snapshot. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reports))

<a id="nestedatt--reports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reports`

Read-Only:

- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the report is archived.
- `archived_at` (String) When the report was archived (ISO 8601); null for an active report.
- `business_unit_id` (String) Business unit (brand) the report belongs to; `0` is the default business unit.
- `created_at` (String) When the report was created (ISO 8601).
- `created_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the report's creator.
- `description` (String) The report's description (null when unset).
- `id` (String) The report's ID.
- `last_viewed_at` (String) When the report was last viewed (ISO 8601). Volatile — it changes whenever anyone opens the report — so it is excluded from `raw_json`.
- `last_viewed_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the last viewer. Volatile; excluded from `raw_json`.
- `name` (String) The report's name.
- `owner_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the report's owner.
- `permissions` (Attributes) Who can access the report. `type` is one of `PRIVATE`, `EVERYONE_VIEW`, `EVERYONE_EDIT` or `SPECIFIC`; with `SPECIFIC`, list the users/teams in `view` and/or `edit`. Grants are sets (order-insensitive) and are only allowed with `SPECIFIC`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reports--permissions))
- `raw_json` (String) The full API report object as canonical JSON for committed snapshots: sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline, view-tracking fields (`lastViewedAt`, `lastViewedByUserId`) stripped.
- `tags` (Attributes List) Tags on the report (read-only: the API cannot set tags). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reports--tags))
- `updated_at` (String) When the report was last updated (ISO 8601).
- `updated_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the user who last updated the report.

<a id="nestedatt--reports--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reports.permissions`

Read-Only:

- `edit` (Attributes Set) Users/teams granted edit access to the report (`SPECIFIC` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reports--permissions--edit))
- `type` (String) Permission type.
- `view` (Attributes Set) Users/teams granted view access to the report (`SPECIFIC` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reports--permissions--view))

<a id="nestedatt--reports--permissions--edit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reports.permissions.edit`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) HubSpot user ID or team ID.
- `type` (String) Grantee kind: `USER` or `TEAM`.


<a id="nestedatt--reports--permissions--view"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reports.permissions.view`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) HubSpot user ID or team ID.
- `type` (String) Grantee kind: `USER` or `TEAM`.



<a id="nestedatt--reports--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reports.tags`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Tag ID.
- `name` (String) Tag name.
